16	# Step 5 — Iterative Refinement
17	
18	Step 4 全部章节落盘后，Paper Agent 进入 Step 5：把全文递交 Reviewer 评分，按反馈修改，直到收敛。
19	
20	**核心约束**：
21	- 串行——一轮 Reviewer 返回结果处理完才进下一轮，禁止并发请求
22	- 评分驱动——overall 提升才 accept 本轮，下降则 git revert
23	- 上限 5 轮——硬约束，达到上限即停，不论分数
24	
25	## 状态记录（git 是 truth source）
26	
27	每轮修改前 commit 当前论文目录，作为 revert 锚点。无需额外 state 文件。
28	
29	```
30	git -C projects/{project} add paper/
31	git -C projects/{project} commit -m "[paper] refinement round {N-1}"
32	```
33	
34	Round N 的 commit message 用 `N-1`，即 round 1 修改前 commit `round 0`（Step 4 落盘后的初稿）。
35	
36	## 单轮流程
37	
38	```
39	Round N（N = 1..5）：
40	
41	1. git commit 当前版本（message: "[paper] refinement round N-1"）
42	   └── 落地评分下降时的 revert 锚点
43	
44	2. 组装审查请求：
45	   - read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml") — 用户自定义必查项
46	   - 拼 LaTeX 全文（或 Patch 模式下的差异）+ writing_plan.yaml 路径
47	   - 末尾追加 "## 用户自定义必查项"（见下方"checklist 注入格式"）
48	
49	3. paper_agent_request_review(text=组装后的请求, project=...)
50	   └── Reviewer 通过 reviewer_post_to_director 回传评分
51	
52	4. 解析 Reviewer 响应：
53	   - 维度分（Originality/Clarity/Soundness/Significance/Presentation，1-4）
54	   - overall（1-10）
55	   - 各条具体问题 severity（critical/warning/info）
56	   - checklist 项 PASS/FAIL
57	   ★ 任一 checklist FAIL → 该条问题 severity 自动按 critical 对待
58	
59	5. 按问题类型分流处理：
60	   - 事实性错误（数字不一致 / 引用错位）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section 改
61	   - 段落级叙事问题（逻辑断裂 / 强度词超限）→ spawn Worker 重写段落，回来再 edit_paper_section
62	   - 结构问题（章节顺序 / 段落归并）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section
63	   - critical 且 claim 本身无支撑 → 汇报 Director（不要自行降 claim）
64	
65	6. 全部问题处理完后判断本轮 overall 走势：
66	   - overall(N) ≥ overall(N-1) → 保留本轮修改，进入收敛判断
67	   - overall(N) <  overall(N-1) → git checkout 上一轮 commit，回退本轮所有修改，标记"本轮无进展"
68	
69	7. 收敛判断（任一满足即停）：
70	   - 全部问题为 info（无 critical / warning）
71	   - N == 5（硬上限）
72	   - 连续两轮 overall 持平（差 ≤0.1）
73	   - 连续两轮无新增 critical（critical 列表内容相同或更短）
74	
75	   未收敛且 N<5 → 进入 Round N+1
76	   已收敛 → 进入收尾（见下文）
77	```
78	
79	## checklist 注入格式
80	
81	`read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml")` 拿到 items 后，在审查请求末尾追加：
82	
83	```
84	## 用户自定义必查项
85	以下是用户指定的必须检查的项，每项必须明确标注 PASS 或 FAIL：
86	- [chk_001] {text}
87	- [chk_002] {text}
88	...
89	
90	如果任何一项标注为 FAIL，整体 severity 自动提升为 critical（必须打回修改）。
91	```
92	
93	- checklist 为空 / 文件不存在 → 不追加该段，正常请求
94	- 不要重写 checklist 文本——保持用户原话，让 Reviewer 自己定位
95	- Dream 模式禁止注入（Dream 论文不投，格式检查无意义）
96	
97	## 修改 Worker 任务模板
98	
99	段落级修改派 Worker（不是整章重写）时：
100	
101	```
102	spawn_worker(
103	  task_type="paper_writing",
104	  project=...,
105	  task_prompt="""
106	Reviewer 在 {section} 章发现以下问题，需要你修改对应段落：
107	
108	【问题位置】{paragraph_id / 行号}
109	【问题描述】{Reviewer 原文}
110	【建议方向】{Reviewer 给的方向}
111	
112	当前段落原文：
113	```latex
114	{原文片段}
115	```
116	
117	参考资料：
118	- 写作规范：Read skills/global/latex-paper.skill.md + red-section.skill.md
119	- registry 切片：{相关 exp_id 列表}
120	- 同章节已有内容：{section}.tex 整章
121	- 引用：references.bib（只用已 verified 条目，未验证标 [UNVERIFIED]）
122	
123	要求：
124	- 只改问题段落，不动其他内容
125	- 输出修改后的段落 latex（标记 old / new）
126	- 不要画图、不要补实验
127	- 改完即返回，不写额外说明
128	"""
129	)
130	```
131	
132	Worker 返回后 Paper Agent 用 `edit_paper_section(project, section, old_text=..., new_text=..., claims=..., table_cells=..., figures=...)` 落盘——`edit_paper_section` 自动同步 provenance，不会 deprecate 未触及的 claim。
133	
134	## 收敛后收尾（Step 5e）
135	
136	Reviewer 评分循环收敛后**必须执行完整三件套**——视觉 + 引用 + 溯源**全部跑完**再汇报 Director；不允许只跑一两项就提交。任一发现 critical/blocker 都要在汇报中显式列出，不得"建议提交审稿"压过失败信号。
137	
138	### 三件套执行顺序
139	
140	按下面顺序串行（每一步完成才进下一步，前一步失败不绕过）：
141	
142	```
143	1. paper-visual-review 排版检查
144	   └── Read skills/global/paper-visual-review.skill.md
145	   └── pdf_to_images(pdf_path=projects/{project}/paper/main.pdf, pages="1-N", dpi=200)
146	       逐页检查图表分辨率 / 字号 / 边距溢出 / 公式 / 引用编号 / 缺失引用占位 [?]
147	   └── cleanup_pdf_images(output_dir=<上一步返回的 output_dir>)  # 不留临时文件
148	   └── 收集 findings：[{page, severity, issue}]
149	   └── 出现 critical（图表溢出 / 缺失编号 / 公式乱码）→ 记入 visual_report，**不**立即返工，
150	       与 verify_references / check_provenance_completeness 的结果**一并汇报 Director**
151	
152	2. verify_references 最终引用验证
153	   └── verify_references(paper_dir="projects/{project}/paper", project=..., skip_online=False)
154	   └── 返回字段：status (ok/orphan_bib/missing_bib/not_found/mismatch) 按条聚合
155	   └── critical 阈值：
156	        - missing_bib（正文 \cite 但 .bib 缺）→ 必须修，否则 LaTeX 编译失败
157	        - not_found（OpenAlex 找不到）→ 疑似幻觉引用，自己 WebSearch 二次验证；仍找不到 → critical
158	        - mismatch（年份/作者偏差）→ warning
159	   └── 自己能改的小问题（missing_bib、年份） → edit_paper_section 修；改完**再调一次 verify_references** 确认通过
160	
161	3. check_provenance_completeness 溯源覆盖
162	   └── check_provenance_completeness(project=...)
163	   └── 返回：tier_distribution / untracked_numbers / invalidated_claims
164	   └── 关键阈值：
165	        - Tier 3 占比 > 30% → 必须汇报 Director（红线，不得静默交付）
166	        - Tier X（invalidated，实验失败/被作废）≥ 1 条 → critical：claim 失去支撑，汇报 Director 决策是否改 claim
167	        - untracked_numbers（正文出现但 provenance 没追踪的数字）≥ 5 → warning：派 Worker 补 provenance
168	```
169	
170	### 汇报 Director 模板
171	
172	三件套全部跑完后**统一**汇报（不要分三次发），把所有 critical/warning 列在一处便于 Director 决策：
173	
174	```
175	paper_agent_post_to_director(
176	  text="[写作进展] Step 5 收尾完成
177	         迭代轮数：{N}/5
178	         最终 overall：{score}
179	         checklist：全部 PASS / 还有 X 条 FAIL（已修复 / 待 Director 决策）
180	
181	         ===== 视觉检查 =====
182	         检查页数：{n}/{total}
183	         结论：PASS / 发现 X 条 critical + Y 条 warning
184	         {若有 critical：逐条列出 page + 描述}
185	
186	         ===== 引用验证 =====
187	         总数 X 条，已验证 Y 条
188	         critical：missing_bib X 条 + 疑似幻觉 Y 条（已尝试 WebSearch 二次验证 → 结果）
189	         warning：mismatch X 条
190	         {若有 critical：列出条目 + 已采取的修复}
191	
192	         ===== Provenance 覆盖 =====
193	         Tier 分布：T1 {a}% / T2 {b}% / T3 {c}% / TX {d}%
194	         {若 T3 > 30% 或 TX ≥ 1：列出受影响的 claim/figure/table}
195	         未追踪数字：X 个（详见 untracked_numbers）
196	
197	         ===== 建议 =====
198	         {以下任选其一}
199	         A. 视觉/引用/provenance 全部 PASS → 建议提交审稿（submit_paper_to_review）
200	         B. 存在 critical → 请 Director 决策：{具体问题列表 + 建议修复方向}
201	         C. provenance 红线触发 → 请 Director 决定：补实验 / 改 claim / 接受现状",
202	  project=...
203	)
204	```
205	
206	Director 决定是否调 `submit_paper_to_review`——Paper Agent **不**主动调，这是 Director 的权限。
207	
208	### 红线（Step 5e 不可绕过）
209	
210	1. **三件套必须全跑**：跳过任一项直接汇报 = 违规，被 Director 打回时不接受"我以为不必要"
211	2. **critical 不静默**：视觉 critical / verify_references critical / Tier X ≥ 1 / Tier 3 > 30% 必须显式写进汇报
212	3. **不主动提交审稿**：哪怕全 PASS 也只能"建议提交"，submit_paper_to_review 是 Director 权限
213	4. **修复后必须复验**：自己修了 missing_bib → 重跑 verify_references；补 provenance → 重跑 check_provenance_completeness
214	5. **Patch 模式走 Phase E**：Patch 的收尾在 Phase E（max 3 轮 Reviewer），不复用 Step 5e 全套；Phase E 自己做 check_provenance_completeness + verify_references，视觉检查可选
215	
216	## 硬约束（与 Paper Agent 红线一致）
217	
218	1. **修改前必 git commit**——没有 commit 不开新一轮，避免 revert 失败
219	2. **未验证引用不进 .bib**——Reviewer 指出新引用需求时，先 verify_references 再写入
220	3. **checklist FAIL 项必须修复**——不参与"连续两轮无新增 critical"的轮数计数，但下一轮必须解决
221	4. **overall 下降必 revert**——不允许"将就一下"
222	5. **不自行降 claim**——claim 无支撑是 Director 决策，Paper Agent 只能改表述强度，不能改 claim 内容
223	6. **Patch / Dream 模式不走本 skill**——Patch 走 Phase E（max 3 轮），Dream 跳过 Reviewer 迭代
224	
225	## 与 Reviewer 评分模板的合约
226	
227	Reviewer 在 `prompts/roles/reviewer.md` §5.3 已规定返回格式：
228	
229	```
230	[写作评审] 轮次 N/5
231	维度评分（1-4）：Originality / Clarity / Soundness / Significance / Presentation
232	Overall（1-10）：
233	## 用户自定义必查项（如审查请求含 paper_checklist）
234	- [chk_id]: PASS / FAIL — 理由
235	## 具体问题
236	- [severity] 位置 + 描述 + 建议
237	```
238	
239	Paper Agent 解析时按位置抓字段——Reviewer 偶尔会漏维度分，**漏了的当作 4（满分）处理**，避免误判 overall 下降。

# Step 5 — Iterative Refinement

Step 4 全部章节落盘后，Paper Agent 进入 Step 5：把全文递交 Reviewer 评分，按反馈修改，直到收敛。

**核心约束**：
- 串行——一轮 Reviewer 返回结果处理完才进下一轮，禁止并发请求
- 评分驱动——overall 提升才 accept 本轮，下降则 git revert
- 上限 5 轮——硬约束，达到上限即停，不论分数

## 状态记录（git 是 truth source）

每轮修改前 commit 当前论文目录，作为 revert 锚点。无需额外 state 文件。

```
git -C projects/{project} add paper/
git -C projects/{project} commit -m "[paper] refinement round {N-1}"
```

Round N 的 commit message 用 `N-1`，即 round 1 修改前 commit `round 0`（Step 4 落盘后的初稿）。

## 单轮流程

```
Round N（N = 1..5）：

1. git commit 当前版本（message: "[paper] refinement round N-1"）
   └── 落地评分下降时的 revert 锚点

2. 组装审查请求：
   - read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml") — 用户自定义必查项
   - 拼 LaTeX 全文（或 Patch 模式下的差异）+ writing_plan.yaml 路径
   - 末尾追加 "## 用户自定义必查项"（见下方"checklist 注入格式"）

3. paper_agent_request_review(text=组装后的请求, project=...)
   └── Reviewer 通过 reviewer_post_to_director 回传评分

4. 解析 Reviewer 响应：
   - 维度分（Originality/Clarity/Soundness/Significance/Presentation，1-4）
   - overall（1-10）
   - 各条具体问题 severity（critical/warning/info）
   - checklist 项 PASS/FAIL
   ★ 任一 checklist FAIL → 该条问题 severity 自动按 critical 对待

5. 按问题类型分流处理：
   - 事实性错误（数字不一致 / 引用错位）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section 改
   - 段落级叙事问题（逻辑断裂 / 强度词超限）→ spawn Worker 重写段落，回来再 edit_paper_section
   - 结构问题（章节顺序 / 段落归并）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section
   - critical 且 claim 本身无支撑 → 汇报 Director（不要自行降 claim）

6. 全部问题处理完后判断本轮 overall 走势：
   - overall(N) ≥ overall(N-1) → 保留本轮修改，进入收敛判断
   - overall(N) <  overall(N-1) → git checkout 上一轮 commit，回退本轮所有修改，标记"本轮无进展"

7. 收敛判断（任一满足即停）：
   - 全部问题为 info（无 critical / warning）
   - N == 5（硬上限）
   - 连续两轮 overall 持平（差 ≤0.1）
   - 连续两轮无新增 critical（critical 列表内容相同或更短）

   未收敛且 N<5 → 进入 Round N+1
   已收敛 → 进入收尾（见下文）
```

## checklist 注入格式

`read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml")` 拿到 items 后，在审查请求末尾追加：

```
## 用户自定义必查项
以下是用户指定的必须检查的项，每项必须明确标注 PASS 或 FAIL：
- [chk_001] {text}
- [chk_002] {text}
...

如果任何一项标注为 FAIL，整体 severity 自动提升为 critical（必须打回修改）。
```

- checklist 为空 / 文件不存在 → 不追加该段，正常请求
- 不要重写 checklist 文本——保持用户原话，让 Reviewer 自己定位
- Dream 模式禁止注入（Dream 论文不投，格式检查无意义）

## 修改 Worker 任务模板

段落级修改派 Worker（不是整章重写）时：

```
spawn_worker(
  task_type="paper_writing",
  project=...,
  task_prompt="""
Reviewer 在 {section} 章发现以下问题，需要你修改对应段落：

【问题位置】{paragraph_id / 行号}
【问题描述】{Reviewer 原文}
【建议方向】{Reviewer 给的方向}

当前段落原文：
```latex
{原文片段}
```

参考资料：
- 写作规范：Read skills/global/latex-paper.skill.md + red-section.skill.md
- registry 切片：{相关 exp_id 列表}
- 同章节已有内容：{section}.tex 整章
- 引用：references.bib（只用已 verified 条目，未验证标 [UNVERIFIED]）

要求：
- 只改问题段落，不动其他内容
- 输出修改后的段落 latex（标记 old / new）
- 不要画图、不要补实验
- 改完即返回，不写额外说明
"""
)
```

Worker 返回后 Paper Agent 用 `edit_paper_section(project, section, old_text=..., new_text=..., claims=..., table_cells=..., figures=...)` 落盘——`edit_paper_section` 自动同步 provenance，不会 deprecate 未触及的 claim。

## 收敛后收尾（Step 5e）

Reviewer 评分循环收敛后**必须执行完整三件套**——视觉 + 引用 + 溯源**全部跑完**再汇报 Director；不允许只跑一两项就提交。任一发现 critical/blocker 都要在汇报中显式列出，不得"建议提交审稿"压过失败信号。

### 三件套执行顺序

按下面顺序串行（每一步完成才进下一步，前一步失败不绕过）：

```
1. paper-visual-review 排版检查
   └── Read skills/global/paper-visual-review.skill.md
   └── pdf_to_images(pdf_path=projects/{project}/paper/main.pdf, pages="1-N", dpi=200)
       逐页检查图表分辨率 / 字号 / 边距溢出 / 公式 / 引用编号 / 缺失引用占位 [?]
   └── cleanup_pdf_images(output_dir=<上一步返回的 output_dir>)  # 不留临时文件
   └── 收集 findings：[{page, severity, issue}]
   └── 出现 critical（图表溢出 / 缺失编号 / 公式乱码）→ 记入 visual_report，**不**立即返工，
       与 verify_references / check_provenance_completeness 的结果**一并汇报 Director**

2. verify_references 最终引用验证
   └── verify_references(paper_dir="projects/{project}/paper", project=..., skip_online=False)
   └── 返回字段：status (ok/orphan_bib/missing_bib/not_found/mismatch) 按条聚合
   └── critical 阈值：
        - missing_bib（正文 \cite 但 .bib 缺）→ 必须修，否则 LaTeX 编译失败
        - not_found（OpenAlex 找不到）→ 疑似幻觉引用，自己 WebSearch 二次验证；仍找不到 → critical
        - mismatch（年份/作者偏差）→ warning
   └── 自己能改的小问题（missing_bib、年份） → edit_paper_section 修；改完**再调一次 verify_references** 确认通过

3. check_provenance_completeness 溯源覆盖
   └── check_provenance_completeness(project=...)
   └── 返回：tier_distribution / untracked_numbers / invalidated_claims
   └── 关键阈值：
        - Tier 3 占比 > 30% → 必须汇报 Director（红线，不得静默交付）
        - Tier X（invalidated，实验失败/被作废）≥ 1 条 → critical：claim 失去支撑，汇报 Director 决策是否改 claim
        - untracked_numbers（正文出现但 provenance 没追踪的数字）≥ 5 → warning：派 Worker 补 provenance
```

### 汇报 Director 模板

Larger models may produce higher-quality and more diverse samples, potentially altering the signal landscape.

### Abstract
Test-time scaling through repeated sampling promises quality gains for LLM-based information extraction (IE), but whether confidence signals can identify the best output among multiple candidates remains untested for structured tasks.
We compare five confidence signals across NER and relation extraction on three benchmarks with two 8B-parameter model families and uncover a \textit{correlation-selection gap}: signals achieve strong quality estimation yet none significantly improves sample selection despite substantial oracle headroom.
Most signals are instance-level by construction and cannot rank candidates; the empirical question is whether log-probability---the sole per-sample signal---or consensus-proximity selection (MBR decoding) can bridge the gap.
Neither succeeds: log-probability scores are compressed into effective ties, while MBR utility correlates with quality across instances but not within them.

### Introduction (contributions)
C1: A systematic evaluation framework — five signals × three metrics, showing decoupling
C2: The correlation-selection gap and its diagnosis — MBR + LP compression as core empirical contributions, instance-level failure is definitional
C3: Task-complexity boundary conditions — EM/SJ crossover, WNUT-17 collapse, extending Nédellec et al.

Five signals: LP (per-sample, model-internal), EM/FK (surface, instance-level), SJ/VC (structural, instance-level). FK independence: "mild negative dependence" (not positive correlation). Evaluation: ρ + AUROC for QE, best-of-N F1 for selection.

- Robustness: structural > LP across all NER settings; RE only VC > LP (preliminary)

- Two-layer gap: Layer 1 definitional (4/5 instance-level), Layer 2 score compression (intrinsic)
- MBR connection: utility-quality misalignment at per-sample level
- Ablation: free-form LP variance ratio 0.97×, NER selection +0.18pp (negligible); RE LP flips +1.69pp (single seed caveat)

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Self-consistency---sampling multiple outputs and aggregating them---has become a powerful strategy for improving language model reasoning.
On discrete-answer tasks such as arithmetic and commonsense QA, majority voting over chain-of-thought samples yields large gains: +18 percentage points on GSM8K (PaLM-540B; \citealp{wang2023selfconsistency}).
More broadly, test-time compute scaling through repeated sampling and selection has emerged as a complementary axis to model scaling, offering substantial quality improvements at inference time \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.
These results rest on a shared assumption: that among $N$ stochastic samples, a selection mechanism can identify better outputs.
For tasks with a single correct answer, this assumption holds naturally---the majority vote is the selector.
But information extraction (IE) poses a fundamentally different challenge.
The output is not a single token or number; it is a \textit{set} of entities or relations with internal dependencies, where two samples may extract overlapping but non-identical structures.
There is no obvious majority to vote on, partial agreement is the norm rather than the exception, and the space of valid outputs is combinatorially large.
Can self-consistency still provide useful signal in this structured setting?

Prior work on confidence estimation for LLM-based IE has conflated two distinct objectives: \textit{quality estimation} (which inputs does the model handle reliably?) and \textit{sample selection} (which of $N$ outputs is best?).
These require fundamentally different signal properties: the former benefits from instance-level aggregation, while the latter demands per-sample discrimination.
Self-consistency methods for discrete answers \cite{wang2023selfconsistency, chen2024usc} and weighted variants \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty} assume outputs can be grouped by equivalence---an assumption that breaks for entity sets with partial overlap.
The most relevant study, \citet{nedellec2026consistency}, examines consistency--accuracy correlations for LLM-based IE, finding results that our quality-estimation analysis corroborates.
Our work extends theirs in three directions: (i)~structural matching beyond surface-level agreement, (ii)~testing whether quality estimation translates to best-of-$N$ selection (it does not), and (iii)~a difficulty gradient revealing non-obvious findings---WNUT-17 conditional correlations collapse to $\rho{=}0.038$ (n.s.) and LP exhibits strong \textit{negative} correlation ($\rho{=}{-}0.410$)---that would be invisible on a single dataset.

Structured IE requires schema-compliant output, making constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided} the standard inference strategy---without it, a substantial fraction of outputs from general-purpose models are unparseable.\footnote{Fine-tuned models may retain format compliance without grammar constraints: our free-form ablation achieves 99.95\% valid JSON rate (\S\ref{sec:ablation}).}
All experiments use constrained decoding, the regime under which structured IE is practically deployed.

Our central finding is the \textbf{correlation-selection gap} (Figure~\ref{fig:overview}): consistency-based signals achieve strong quality estimation ($\rho$ up to 0.38, AUROC up to 0.75) but fail at sample selection despite 13--18~pp of oracle headroom.
Four of five signals are instance-level by construction---this is definitional, not empirical.
The non-trivial questions are whether (a)~consensus-proximity selection, instantiating MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, freitag2022high, muller2021understanding}, can recover per-sample discrimination, and (b)~whether log-probability, the only per-sample signal, can exploit the headroom.
Both fail: MBR utility correlates with F1 across instances but not within them (\S\ref{sec:discussion}); log-probability scores are severely compressed (60\% of instances effectively tied), though where compression is mitigated, LP becomes a significant selector ($+2.9$~pp, $p{=}0.01$).
A controlled free-form decoding ablation confirms that this compression is intrinsic to the model and task, not an artifact of constrained decoding (\S\ref{sec:ablation}).

\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig_overview}
\caption{The correlation-selection gap. \textbf{Left}: high inter-sample agreement correlates with high F1 (quality estimation). \textbf{Right}: instance-level signals assign identical scores to all candidates, precluding sample selection.}
\label{fig:overview}
\end{figure*}

21	Despite MBR's success in machine translation \cite{freitag2022high} and its extension to summarization, code generation, and captioning \cite{jinnai2024mbr}, all variants fail here because the utility functions correlate with F1 at the instance level but not within a single instance---the mathematical essence of the correlation-selection gap.

Notably, the fine-tuned model achieved 99.95\% parse rate without grammar constraints, suggesting that constrained decoding's format-compliance role may be redundant for sufficiently fine-tuned models.

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Self-consistency---sampling multiple outputs and aggregating them---has become a powerful strategy for improving language model reasoning.
On discrete-answer tasks such as arithmetic and commonsense QA, majority voting over chain-of-thought samples yields large gains: +18 percentage points on GSM8K (PaLM-540B; \citealp{wang2023selfconsistency}).
More broadly, test-time compute scaling through repeated sampling and selection has emerged as a complementary axis to model scaling, offering substantial quality improvements at inference time \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.
These results rest on a shared assumption: that among $N$ stochastic samples, a selection mechanism can identify better outputs.
For tasks with a single correct answer, this assumption holds naturally---the majority vote is the selector.
But information extraction (IE) poses a fundamentally different challenge.
The output is not a single token or number; it is a \textit{set} of entities or relations with internal dependencies, where two samples may extract overlapping but non-identical structures.
There is no obvious majority to vote on, partial agreement is the norm rather than the exception, and the space of valid outputs is combinatorially large.
Can self-consistency still provide useful signal in this structured setting?

Prior work on confidence estimation for LLM-based IE has conflated two distinct objectives: \textit{quality estimation} (which inputs does the model handle reliably?) and \textit{sample selection} (which of $N$ outputs is best?).
These require fundamentally different signal properties: the former benefits from instance-level aggregation, while the latter demands per-sample discrimination.
Self-consistency methods for discrete answers \cite{wang2023selfconsistency, chen2024usc} and weighted variants \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty} assume outputs can be grouped by equivalence---an assumption that breaks for entity sets with partial overlap.
The most relevant study, \citet{nedellec2026consistency}, examines consistency--accuracy correlations for LLM-based IE, finding results that our quality-estimation analysis corroborates.
Our work extends theirs in three directions: (i)~structural matching beyond surface-level agreement, (ii)~testing whether quality estimation translates to best-of-$N$ selection (it does not), and (iii)~a difficulty gradient revealing non-obvious findings---WNUT-17 conditional correlations collapse to $\rho{=}0.038$ (n.s.) and LP exhibits strong \textit{negative} correlation ($\rho{=}{-}0.410$)---that would be invisible on a single dataset.

Structured IE requires schema-compliant output, making constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided} the standard inference strategy---without it, a substantial fraction of outputs from general-purpose models are unparseable.\footnote{Fine-tuned models may retain format compliance without grammar constraints: our free-form ablation achieves 99.95\% valid JSON rate (\S\ref{sec:ablation}).}
All experiments use constrained decoding, the regime under which structured IE is practically deployed.

Our central finding is the \textbf{correlation-selection gap} (Figure~\ref{fig:overview}): consistency-based signals achieve strong quality estimation ($\rho$ up to 0.38, AUROC up to 0.75) but fail at sample selection despite 13--18~pp of oracle headroom.
Four of five signals are instance-level by construction---this is definitional, not empirical.
The non-trivial questions are whether (a)~consensus-proximity selection, instantiating MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, freitag2022high, muller2021understanding}, can recover per-sample discrimination, and (b)~whether log-probability, the only per-sample signal, can exploit the headroom.
Both fail: MBR utility correlates with F1 across instances but not within them (\S\ref{sec:discussion}); log-probability scores are severely compressed (60\% of instances effectively tied), though where compression is mitigated, LP becomes a significant selector ($+2.9$~pp, $p{=}0.01$).
A controlled free-form decoding ablation confirms that this compression is intrinsic to the model and task, not an artifact of constrained decoding (\S\ref{sec:ablation}).

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig_overview}
\caption{The correlation-selection gap. \textbf{Left}: high inter-sample agreement correlates with high F1 (quality estimation). \textbf{Right}: instance-level signals assign identical scores to all candidates, precluding sample selection.}
\label{fig:overview}
\end{figure*}

We systematically compare five confidence signals from three families---structural (entity voting confidence [VC], Soft Jaccard [SJ]), surface (exact match [EM], Fleiss' $\kappa$ [FK]), and model-internal (log-probability [LP])---across NER and RE on SciERC \cite{luan2018scierc}, CoNLL-2003 \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll}, and WNUT-17 \cite{derczynski2017wnut}, using Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B.
Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Evaluation framework and metric dissociation.}
    We compare five confidence signals from three families---structural, surface, and model-internal---across quality estimation, binary discrimination, and sample selection.
    These metrics decouple: EM leads AUROC (0.749) but ranks third in $\rho$ (0.295), demonstrating that single-metric evaluation risks selecting the wrong signal.

    \item \textbf{Diagnosing why selection fails beyond definitional limitations.}
    Four of five signals are instance-level by definition and cannot rank candidates---this is not an empirical finding.
    The empirical contribution is diagnosing why the two mechanisms that \textit{could} bridge the gap both fail: (a)~consensus-proximity selection (MBR decoding) correlates with quality across instances but not within them; (b)~log-probability scores are compressed into effective ties (60\% of instances within $\varepsilon{=}0.05$), though where compression is mitigated, LP becomes a significant selector ($+2.9$~pp, $p{=}0.01$).
    A controlled NER ablation confirms that LP compression persists without constrained decoding; on RE, LP selection reverses direction (preliminary), suggesting task-dependent interaction with decoding regime.

    \item \textbf{Task-complexity boundary conditions.}
    Signal rankings shift with task difficulty: EM leads on easy tasks, SJ on hard tasks---consistent across two model families at 8B scale, though with model-dependent magnitude.
    At the capability boundary (WNUT-17, 52\% zero F1), conditional correlations collapse to non-significance and LP exhibits strong negative correlation ($\rho{=}{-}0.410$)---phenomena invisible on a single dataset that extend \citet{nedellec2026consistency}'s quality-estimation analysis.
    NER findings span three datasets; RE conclusions rest on SciERC alone (preliminary).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Self-consistency and test-time scaling.}
Self-consistency decoding \cite{wang2023selfconsistency} improves reasoning by majority voting over chain-of-thought samples, assuming a discrete answer space.
Extensions to free-form text use LLM-based comparison \cite{chen2024usc}, atomic sub-claim decomposition \cite{thirukovalluru2024atomic}, or cross-sample hallucination detection \cite{manakul2023selfcheckgpt}.
For test-time scaling \cite{zhang2025tts}, \citet{snell2025scaling} characterize compute scaling laws and \citet{brown2024monkeys} show best-of-$N$ gains across tasks.
Recent reward-free selectors include confidence-weighted voting \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc}, KL-based self-certainty \cite{kang2025selfcertainty}, adaptive sampling \cite{kim2026reasc}, ranked aggregation \cite{wang2025rankedvoting}, and latent-space consistency \cite{oh2025latentsc}.
Concurrently, \citet{feng2025optimal} and \citet{wang2025make} adapt self-consistency to difficulty-aware settings, echoing our finding that signal rankings shift with task complexity; \citet{li2025llms} propose generative self-aggregation for IE but focus on output fusion rather than confidence-based selection.
All of the above target reasoning/QA with discrete answers or specific aggregation strategies.
Our work extends self-consistency to set-valued structured outputs and identifies the correlation-selection gap: strong quality estimation ($\rho{=}0.38$) coexists with selection failure ($p{>}0.39$).

\paragraph{Consistency for structured IE.}
\citet{nedellec2026consistency} study consistency--accuracy correlations for LLM-based NER/RE, corroborating our quality-estimation findings.
Their work leaves open three questions we address: (i)~whether structural matching improves on surface-level agreement (which they acknowledge ``overlooks semantically consistent outputs''); (ii)~whether quality estimation translates to best-of-$N$ selection; and (iii)~whether findings generalize across a difficulty gradient.
Our Soft Jaccard signal addresses (i) through type-aware bipartite matching with token-level span overlap; our selection analysis (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}) directly addresses (ii); and our three-dataset evaluation spanning easy (CoNLL) to hard (SciERC) tasks addresses (iii).
CoCoA \cite{vashurin2025cocoa} fuses model confidence with inter-sample consistency for QA/summarization but does not address structured extraction.
Our evaluation builds on generative IE work \cite{zhou2024uniner, sainz2024gollie, josifoski2022genie, li2023codeie, wadhwa2023revisiting, wang2023instructuie} and constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided}.

\paragraph{Uncertainty estimation and calibration.}
Surveys cover confidence estimation \cite{geng2024confidence}, selective abstention \cite{wen2025know}, uncertainty quantification \cite{xia2025survey}, and calibration \cite{hobelsberger2025systematic} for LLMs; \citet{xiong2024llm} find LLMs tend toward overconfidence, and \citet{heo2025uncertainty} show calibration degrades with task complexity.
Semantic uncertainty \cite{kuhn2023semantic} clusters generations by meaning; \citet{kossen2024semantic} distill this into probes; P(True) \cite{kadavath2022language} queries model confidence directly; \citet{malinin2021uncertainty} distinguish data and model uncertainty in autoregressive models.
Our structural signals instead measure agreement over output \textit{structure}.
Neural networks are often miscalibrated \cite{guo2017calibration, desai2020calibration}; deep ensembles \cite{lakshminarayanan2017ensembles} and MC-dropout \cite{gal2016dropout} obtain uncertainty from model variation, while our approach requires no model modification.
Prior NER uncertainty work spans Bayesian inference for sequence labeling \cite{xiao2019uncertainty}, active learning under uncertainty \cite{shelmanov2021active}, evidential deep learning \cite{zhang2023ener}, verification-augmented NER \cite{kim2024verifiner}, and uncertainty transmission across label sequences \cite{he2024uncertainty}---all within discriminative paradigms.
Conformal prediction \cite{fisch2021conformal, angelopoulos2021conformal} provides coverage guarantees; trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, lightman2024verify, venktesh2025trust} and reward models \cite{wang2024mathshepherd} learn per-sample scoring.
Our selection strategies instantiate MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling} with structural utility functions; despite MBR's success in translation \cite{freitag2022high} and other generation tasks \cite{jinnai2024mbr}, we find utility-quality misalignment at the per-sample level for structured IE (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Selective prediction \cite{geifman2017selective} and confidence-based IE filtering \cite{culotta2004confidence} establish the broader framework.
